messages.text: How Suzuki has wowed Villa fans since replacing Martinez

metadata.summary: Aston Villa fans still sing about having the world's number one goalkeeper. But what started as a chant for Emiliano Martinez and morphed into defiant support for young Japanese goalkeeper Zion Suzuki has become something else. They actually believe it.

Watch Aston Villa vs Fulham live on Saturday Night Football on Sky Sports Premier League; kick-off 8pm Adam Bate Football Features Writer @ghostgoal Friday 30 October 2026 15:16, UK Image: Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki as already made a big impression since joining from Italian club Parma Aston Villa fans still sing about having the world's number one goalkeeper. But what started as a chant for Emiliano Martinez and morphed into defiant support for young Japanese goalkeeper Zion Suzuki has become something else. They actually believe it. Suzuki has been superb since joining from Parma in the summer. Not only has Martinez not been as missed as many anticipated, there is growing optimism that in his 24-year-old replacement, Villa have a goalkeeper who has even more facets to his game. There have been some standout displays already. Suzuki was excellent in the win over Manchester City last time out, ending their 100-per-cent Premier League record under Enzo Maresca. messages.text: Wilkin: Rugby League World Cup format 'fundamentally flawed'

metadata.summary: Sky Sports' Jon Wilkin believes the Rugby League World Cup format is "fundamentally flawed" after England were left on the brink of their first group-stage exit in the tournament's history.
metadata.content: Rugby League World Cup: Jon Wilkin says tournament format is 'fundamentally flawed' as England on brink of historic exit | Rugby League News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Rugby League World Cup: Jon Wilkin says tournament format is 'fundamentally flawed' as England on brink of historic exit England are teetering on the brink of a historic group-stage exit at the Rugby League World Cup despite beating Papua New Guinea on Friday; England need Tonga to defeat Samoa by more than 46 points to advance to the knockout stages Jon Wilkin Rugby League Expert Friday 30 October 2026 16:26, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Jon Wilkin believes the structure of the World Cup was 'fundamentally flawed' Sky Sports' Jon Wilkin believes the Rugby League World Cup format is "fundamentally flawed" after England were left on the brink of their first group-stage exit in the tournament's history. England sealed a 34-12 victory against Papua New Guinea on Friday but needed to win by a margin of 68 points to give themselves a chance of leapfrogging Samoa in Pool B and C and advancing to the semi-finals on points difference. Now their hopes rest on Tonga, who face off against Samoa on Sunday. England need Tonga to win by more than 46 points to secure a spot in the knockout stages. messages.text: Dart into Guangzhou Open semi as Rybakina injured in Tokyo

metadata.summary: Harriet Dart continued her sparkling run at the Guangzhou Open, beating former world No 2 Paula Badosa to reach her second WTA semi-final.
metadata.content: Harriet Dart reaches Guangzhou Open semi-final as Elena Rybakina withdraws with injury at Pan Pacific Open | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Harriet Dart reaches Guangzhou Open semi-final as Elena Rybakina withdraws with injury at Pan Pacific Open Great Britain's Harriet Dart reaches semi-finals of Guangzhou Open; world No 1 Elena Rybakina withdraws from tournament in Japan; watch the WTA and ATP Tours live on Sky Sports Friday 30 October 2026 10:06, UK Image: Harriet Dart has reached the Guangzhou Open semi-finals Harriet Dart continued her sparkling run at the Guangzhou Open, beating former world No 2 Paula Badosa to reach her second WTA semi-final. The British No 3 looked up against it after losing the first set 6-3 but rebounded brilliantly to win the next two sets 6-2 6-4, securing her fifth victory in a row and one of the finest of her career. "It was an incredible battle," Dart said in her on-court interview on Sky Sports. "I thought Paula started really strongly. I was always behind, but I knew going in that it was going to be an incredibly tough match.
